name: Austrian nationalism
summary: Austrian nationalism holds that Austrians are a nation distinct from Germans, with their own cultural unity, Catholic-rooted heritage and an independent state. It arose in opposition to absorption into a Prussian-led or later Nazi Germany, was carried by the Fatherland Front's authoritarian corporatism in 1933-38, and became the Second Republic's national consensus after 1945, expressed in the Anschluss-as-occupation view and permanent neutrality.
scope: The profile represents the post-1945 Austrian-nation idea as the Second Republic consolidated it (separate national history, Anschluss as foreign occupation, permanent neutrality of 1955), with the Catholic cultural core described for Dollfuss and Schuschnigg's Fatherland Front as the historical root. Positions on economics, social issues and democracy are mostly inferred and low-confidence because the nation-concept itself says little about them and the interwar authoritarian strand differs from the postwar democratic one. It excludes pan-German nationalism and the Freedom Party's later German-cultural turn.

keyFigures.name: Engelbert Dollfuss
keyFigures.role: Founder of the Fatherland Front and chancellor who defended Austrian independence against Nazi Germany.

keyFigures.name: Kurt Schuschnigg
keyFigures.role: Dollfuss's successor, who called the 1938 independence referendum and rejected Anschluss.

keyFigures.name: Joseph von Hormayr
keyFigures.role: Napoleonic-era figure named as a leading early Austrian nationalist.

public-ownership.rationale: Postwar Austria nationalised major industry and later privatised much of it, so patriots are split and the sources are silent.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Security-liberty trade-off never addressed by the nationalist idea; adherents split.

strong-leader.rationale: Postwar patriotism is democratic, though the Dollfuss strand ruled by decree and favoured authoritarian leadership, so the strands split.

state-harmful.rationale: No Austrian-nationalist strand is anti-state; a state of Austria's own is the point of the idea.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Legal in practice in Austria while Catholic culture disapproves, so adherents split.

abortion-legal.rationale: Catholic identity pulls against secular Second Republic law; adherents split.

more-religion-public.rationale: Catholic identity was central to the early and interwar nationalism, but postwar patriotism is more secular, hence low.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The movement is defined as cultural nationalism promoting Austrian cultural unity, and postwar proponents built a distinct Austrian cultural history.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Mainstream parties and the FPOe differ; the nation concept as documented does not decide it.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Austria joined the UN while holding neutrality, but nationalists are not clearly for strengthening such bodies.

nation-first.rationale: Neutrality law is framed around preserving Austria's own independence, but the statement is about global cooperation, which Austria also pursues.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Technology optimism is not part of the nation-concept and Catholic-conservative and secular patriots differ.

revolution-justified.rationale: The Fatherland Front crushed the 1934 uprising and Nazi putsch; postwar patriotism is constitutional.

experts-over-public.rationale: The corporatist strand favoured expert bodies while the postwar republic is democratic, leaving adherents split.

socialized-markets.rationale: Postwar nationalised firms and social partnership make this plausible, but the Catholic-conservative strand disagrees; split.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Catholic family-property emphasis points against heavy inheritance tax while social democratic patriots favour it; split.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The 1934 Ständestaat was built on corporatist bodies per Quadragesimo anno, and postwar social partnership continues the idea in milder form. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Fatherland Front was the sole legal party, but postwar Austrian patriotism is multiparty, so strands split and the mainstream answer is no.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Habsburg myth was used in interwar Austria, yet postwar patriots accept the republic; split.

democracy-best.rationale: Second Republic patriotism is democratic, while the Fatherland Front dismantled parliament; mainstream scope but split.

direct-votes.rationale: Austria has limited referendums; the idea itself takes no position and parties differ.

workers-councils.rationale: The Fatherland Front banned Marxist parties and unions, and its corporatism replaced class councils with occupational estates.

natural-rulers.rationale: Authoritarian strand held elite leadership, postwar patriots do not; split.

political-violence-never.rationale: Interwar strand used force against left and Nazis, postwar patriots reject violence; split.

separate-church-state.rationale: Catholic identity and the Fatherland Front's alignment with the Church oppose strict separation; postwar practice is looser.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Austrian nationalism defines the nation by culture and Catholic heritage and argued Austrians were not simply German, so a single-ethnic-group definition is not its basis.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Fatherland Front banned Marxism and sought to unite Austrians beyond class, but the postwar Austrian-nation consensus, the scope's core, included the Socialists and Communists.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Corporatist strand stressed duties, postwar patriots less so; split.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A technical-liberty question the idea never touches, with security-minded and privacy-minded patriots split.

restore-past-order.rationale: The interwar regime evoked Habsburg greatness, but postwar patriotism looks forward; split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Pragmatic social-partnership politics favours results while the Front was openly ideological; split.

means-match-ends.rationale: The statement is a movement-strategy principle without a clear Austrian-nationalist counterpart.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Corporatist estates are organised around distinct occupations, the opposite of abolishing the division of labour.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Fatherland Front outlawed communists and crushed the Social Democrats in 1934.

harm-principle.rationale: The state restricted many private behaviours under Catholic influence yet modern Austria is liberal; split.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The Fatherland Front did not advocate racial ideology, and Austrian nationalism rests on culture rather than race. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

organic-representation.rationale: The 1934 constitution had deputies nominated by corporative councils, which is representation through occupational bodies rather than parties. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

total-state.rationale: The Ständestaat was authoritarian but Catholic and corporative; the postwar state is limited; low because strands split.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Front slogan was Oesterreich, erwache, but the postwar idea is not a rebirth movement; split.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Austrian nationalism is defensive of independence against Anschluss and expansion is alien to it.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Austrian official stance supports Israel's existence but the nation-concept has no line, and strands diverge.

revive-national-language.rationale: German is Austria's language and the idea does not seek a language revival.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The Fatherland Front pursued deflation and austerity while postwar Austria used Keynesian stimulus; split.

economic-freedom.rationale: Social-market patriots accept the link, corporatist ones do not; split.

rule-by-example.rationale: Catholic-corporatist ideas of moral leadership sit alongside the rule-of-law republic; split.

national-self-determination.rationale: The idea is that Austrians form a nation entitled to its own state, and the movement resisted union with Germany in 1938 and earlier.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Fatherland Front aimed to unite Austrians beyond party and class and its corporatism held employers and workers as partners.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Preserving cultural heritage is core to cultural nationalism, so sacrificing museums for novelty is rejected.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Fatherland Front rejected the Marxist view of the state it suppressed in 1934.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Austria has little domestic fossil output and patriots split between energy security and environmental pride.

elite-replacement.rationale: Fringe conspiratorial theory outside the documented core; not typical.

proportional-representation.rationale: Austria uses PR but the idea is indifferent; the Front abolished elections.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Postwar Austria long avoided accountability, then reversed after Waldheim; adherents split.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Racial ideology was not part of the Austrian nation concept; Front did not adopt it. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The Fatherland Front's state required religious instruction through the Matura; postwar Austria has confessional religious teaching.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist doctrine rejected by the Front, and unrelated to neutrality.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Postwar Austrian nation rests on an independent democratic republic; the interwar regime less so, hence low.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist goals are not part of the nationalism and Austria's economy is open; split.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Neutrality is defensive but the statement is absolute and libertarian.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The Fatherland Front banned the Austrian Nazi and Communist parties to defend the state, and postwar patriots likewise outlaw Nazi revival.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional Austria keeps separated powers while the 1934 regime concentrated them; split.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Front banned communists and opposed Marxist-Leninist parties.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Catholic social teaching supports it, but the idea is not defined by it.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Vienna's municipal housing is a source of local pride on the left and criticised on the right; split.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Fatherland Front dissolved free unions, postwar patriots accept strikes; split.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Cultural unity is central but sources do not link it to diversity directly; split.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Dollfuss ruled by emergency decree while postwar patriots oppose; split.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Austria used price controls after wars but the idea takes no line; split.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Strong party discipline exists in Austrian parties but the idea is silent; split.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Neutrality law forbids military alliances yet Austria joined the EU; patriots are split.

clerical-rule.rationale: The regime was Catholic-aligned but run by politicians, not clerics.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The Front opposed Marxist revolutionary defeatism and defended national independence.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Catholic voices favoured censorship, liberal patriots oppose; split.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The Front's authoritarian leadership had no term limits while the republic has them; split.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Austria has pledged never to join alliances or host bases, which is the neutrality position, though this statement concerns ending existing ones.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Austrians reject union with Germany even though language is shared, so reunification is not the model.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Populist patriots say yes while mainstream ones do not; the idea is silent.

death-penalty.rationale: Austria abolished it and mainstream patriots accept; not in sources.

minority-language-support.rationale: Austria recognises minority languages (Slovene, Croatian, Hungarian) per the Wikipedia article on nationalism.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Catholic identity favours accommodation but the nation emphasises common law; split.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Austrian president is directly elected, but the idea does not require it.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Catholic social teaching in Quadragesimo anno, adopted by the corporatist state, subordinates property to common good. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

collective-defense.rationale: Austria pledged never to join military alliances, which rules out automatic collective defence.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Postwar Austria held that the 1938 Anschluss was an unlawful occupation, as in the Moscow Declaration and the 1945 proclamation.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: No Austrian-nationalist stance and Austria avoids force abroad; split.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Austria's federalism allows autonomy but the idea has no stance on joining a larger state.

character-from-environment.rationale: Catholic and social-democratic traditions differ on nature versus nurture; split.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Corporatist estates recall mixed constitutions yet the republic is parliamentary; split.

leader-cult.rationale: The Front was authoritarian but sources do not describe a leader cult; postwar patriots reject.

equal-parenting.rationale: Catholic-conservative patriots resist while modern law moves toward it; split.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis the Front rejected as part of Marxism.

refugee-return.rationale: Austria took refugees after 1945 and the idea does not address return rights; split.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Austrian nationalism opposed absorbing Austria into Germany for shared nationality, and seeks no claims abroad.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The idea is that Austrians are a nation apart from Germans despite shared language, and it opposed the Anschluss.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The Fatherland Front opposed Marxism, which asserts this historical materialism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Corporatism accepts organised economic bodies while social-market patriots favour competition; split.

no-bailouts.rationale: Austria has bailed out banks and firms; the idea has no stance and patriots split.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Front crushed the 1934 uprising and a Nazi putsch, and rejects revolutionary violence.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Austria abolished nobility titles in 1919 and nostalgia for Habsburgs exists; split.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Postwar historians built a separate Austrian national history with its own heroes.

patriotic-education.rationale: The postwar nation-building programme promoted Austrian identity and history, such as the 1946 Ostarrichi celebrations.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Marxist collapse question; the Front and social partnership both regarded capitalism as reformable, so unclear.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Habsburg heritage is valued, but there is no stated aim of influence in former lands; split.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis the Front opposed.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Austria's constitution includes basic rights but the idea does not address this.

elective-rulers.rationale: Republic elects, but the Front and monarchist nostalgia complicate.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Austrian history holds both obedience to authority and resistance to Nazi rule; split.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Postwar patriots say yes while the 1934 regime abolished parliament; split.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A critical-theory claim outside the idea; patriots split.

native-born-offices.rationale: Austria restricts some offices to citizens; native-born only is not typical.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Postwar Austria condemned Nazism but the Front itself called Austrofascist; split.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The Front opposed both Nazis and Marxists in a two-front war, implying equal condemnation.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Cultural heritage preservation points yes while the postwar break with Nazism points no; split.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: A gender-politics debate outside the idea; patriots split.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: A gender-politics debate outside the idea; patriots split.

paid-care-work.rationale: Catholic family policy and social-democratic welfare differ; split.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Austria screens some foreign takeovers and the idea is silent; split.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Catholic-conservative and secular patriots disagree; split.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The postwar republic requires it while Dollfuss ruled by decree; split.

single-official-language.rationale: German is the state language yet Austria recognises minority languages.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The Front framed austerity as Catholic modesty against consumerism.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Contrary to permanent neutrality and non-interference.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Contrary to Austria's own experience of external annexation and its neutrality.

corporate-influence.rationale: Social partnership gives organised interests a formal role, so views are mixed.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Sovereignty arguments by nationalists compete with free-association norms; split.

job-guarantee.rationale: Corporatist and social-democratic strands lean yes, market-oriented patriots no; split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Austria's ÖGB is organised by industry, but the idea has no stance.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The Fatherland Front did not advocate racial ideology and incorporated a Jewish veterans league. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Neutrality is a domestic constitutional law, but Austria also accepts EU and international law; split.

religious-nation.rationale: Catholic identity was central to early Austrian nationalism but the postwar nation is not defined by religion alone; split.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Contrary to independence, which the nationalism centres on.

defeat-communism.rationale: The Front banned communists but postwar neutral Austria coexisted with the Soviet bloc.

religion-illusion.rationale: Catholic identity is central to the early nationalism and the Front opposed Marxist atheism.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Corporatists were critical of capitalism, while market patriots are favourable; split.

majority-settlement.rationale: Contrary to Austria's recognition of minority languages and regions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Fatherland Front rejected both laissez-faire capitalism and Marxism and claimed a Catholic corporatist third course. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Austria has no major claim apart from occasional South Tyrol sentiment; split.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Postwar Austria abandoned the victim myth and bans denial; sources silent on denial itself.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Interwar regime suppressed opposition; postwar patriots do not; split.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Austria retains a blasphemy-type law yet patriots disagree on it; split.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Austria has some participatory features but the idea has no stance.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Legal recognition exists in Austria, while Catholic-conservative patriots resist; split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Fatherland Front claimed to transcend parties; postwar patriots split.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept the Front rejected.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Populist patriots say yes and mainstream patriots do not, and Austria recognised Islam in 1912.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Catholic cultural patriots and secular patriots differ; split.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The neutrality law commits Austria to defend its neutrality with all means at its disposal.

rich-first.rationale: A Chinese development doctrine with no Austrian-nationalist counterpart.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The 1955 constitutional law declares permanent neutrality and bars joining military alliances.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The Front itself practised austerity while patriots split on IMF conditions.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept the Front rejected.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: A Marxist critique the Front rejected.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule of law is accepted in the republic though Dollfuss ruled by decree; split.

racial-franchise.rationale: Austrian nationalism did not rest on race; Front rejected racial ideology. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The Front did not adopt antisemitic racial ideology and incorporated a Jewish front-soldiers league. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Catholic social teaching warns of concentration while corporatist patriots accept wealth; split.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Austria permits it and patriots do not object strongly; split.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Catholic identity is central to the early nationalism, and the Front opposed Marxist atheism.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Postwar Austria used grand coalitions and proporz power-sharing, but it is not a doctrine of the idea.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Catholic subsidiarity favours charity while Austrian social partnership favours state provision; split.

term-limits.rationale: Austria limits the presidency but not parliament; the idea has no stance.

rent-control.rationale: Austrian tenant protection is long established but contested; split.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Front had recreational organization modelled on Strength Through Joy; no drilled youth documented; split.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The neutrality law says Austria will never permit foreign military bases on its territory.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Austria recognised the Holocaust after 1988 but the idea has no stance on other cases; split.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Catholic social teaching stresses reward for work but accepts ownership returns; split.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Neutrality is to be defended by arms, so self-defence is legitimate.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Postwar proponents stressed Celtic, Illyrian and Roman roots and the Ostarrichi anniversary to give Austria deep continuity.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Dollfuss was honoured as a martyr by the Front; postwar view split.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Catholic strand framed politics partly spiritually, but postwar patriots do not; split.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: No diaspora-centred doctrine in the Austrian idea.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Cultural nationalists may favour it, but the nation is not defined by ethnic majority; split.

independent-unions.rationale: Postwar unions independent, Front absorbed them; split.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A Marxist test the Front rejected.

person-over-state.rationale: Catholic personalism supports it while the corporatist state subordinated persons; split.

dense-cities.rationale: The idea has no stance; patriots split between rural and urban pride.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Austrian nationalism rests on culture and Catholic heritage, and the Front did not adopt racial ideology. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Neutrality law aims at independence and inviolability of territory.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Austrians share German with Germany yet constitute a separate nation, so language does not define the nation.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Austria has no current partition narrative; the idea has none.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Catholic-conservative adherents accept distinct roles but may not call this political; split.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Neutral Austria hosts diplomacy but the idea has no stance on secrecy.

smash-state-machine.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist idea opposed by the Front.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Fatherland Front banned party competition and the postwar consensus favoured broad national parties, so a separate workers' party is not a core aim.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Adherents are split; the nation-concept says little about environment versus liberty.

voter-id.rationale: The nation concept is silent on voter identification; adherents are not split along nationalist lines.

premarital-sex.rationale: The Catholic cultural root points against, the secular Second Republic points for; adherents are split and the sources are silent.

national-church-status.rationale: The Fatherland Front privileged the Catholic Church, but the postwar Republic treats churches under a concordat without a formal state church; strands differ.

equal-conscription.rationale: Austria keeps male-only conscription tied to its neutrality, but the nation-concept takes no stated position on gender equality in it.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Adherents are split: Austrian nationalism defined itself against pan-German claims, and South Tyrol is the main case.

multipolar-world.rationale: The 1955 neutrality law and the idea of a small independent state lean to a world of several independent powers and non-alignment.

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: Habsburg heritage is valued, but there is no stated aim of influence in former lands; split. (Carried over from former-empire-influence, "A country should cultivate political and cultural influence in regions once ruled by its predecessor empire.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: A country's permanent military neutrality should be written into its constitution.
missingStatements.rationale: Austria's 1955 constitutional law declares permanent neutrality, which became a pillar of the postwar Austrian nation.

missingStatements.text: A people who share a language with a neighbouring country can still form a separate nation with its own state.
missingStatements.rationale: Austrian nationalism rests on the claim that Austrians are a nation distinct from Germans despite a common language, in opposition to Anschluss.

notes: Interwar Fatherland Front strand (authoritarian, one-party, corporatist) and postwar democratic strand answer differently on political-system statements, so those are low confidence. The Freedom Party's partial claim to the tradition is not represented.
